angle: LEGO is now a toy giant, but in 2004 it was losing money fast: DKK 6.3 billion of sales and a DKK 1.8 billion loss. Its own annual reports trace the curve since: DKK 83.5 billion of revenue in 2025, 13 times more, and a DKK 16.7 billion net profit, more than two and a half times everything it sold in 2004.
paragraphs: In {two thousand four|2004}, LEGO was in trouble.
Sales had shrunk to {six point three billion|6.3 billion} kroner. And it lost {one point eight billion|1.8 billion}.
Then it went back to the brick.
By {twenty sixteen|2016}, sales were almost {thirty-eight billion|38 billion}.
In {twenty twenty-five|2025}: {eighty-three point five billion|83.5 billion}. Thirteen times more.
Profit went from a {one point eight billion|1.8 billion} loss to a {sixteen point seven billion|16.7 billion} profit.
That's over two and a half times its entire sales in {two thousand four|2004}.
Last year, shoppers spent {sixteen percent|16%} more on LEGO, over twice the toy market's pace.
LEGO used to lose money. Now its profit beats its old sales. More on the channel.
